name: Quadrilateral Space Syndrome
definition: Compression of the axillary nerve and/or posterior circumflex humeral artery in the quadrilateral space, usually producing posterior shoulder pain and deltoid/teres minor dysfunction.

investigations.principle: MRI can show teres minor denervation; electrodiagnostics and vascular imaging are selective.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, cartilage, ligament or occult injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent objective compression may require decompression.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

patientEducation.summary: Compression of the axillary nerve and/or posterior circumflex humeral artery in the quadrilateral space, usually producing posterior shoulder pain and deltoid/teres minor dysfunction.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, unreduced dislocation, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
